::: {.entry-meta}
[decision]{.chip .decision} [measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 81 · milestone JOREK (alongside M4)
:::

[Entry 75](75-time-step-check-of-the-case-b-pedestal-modes.qmd) showed that the growth rates of
the three case (b) pedestal modes, n = 12, 16 and 20, do not change when the time step is
halved. Decision 7 also asks for the grid to be doubled. Four ways of doing that were put to
the owner ([OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43)). The owner chose the most expensive one: run all three modes again on the
doubled grid, 160 × 256, starting from round-off as on the original grid. This entry
describes how that check is set up and what it costs. The result will follow in a later entry.

## Method

The grid is the only change. Each mode starts from the doubled-grid axisymmetric state made
in entry 75, and has to rise from round-off again. On the original grid that took several
thousand time steps, far more than one six-hour job covers. The check is therefore a chain of
jobs, each restarting every mode from its own latest saved state. Two rules were fixed before
any step on the doubled grid ran, with every input recorded by checksum:
- **Comparison.** The window rule of entry 73 is applied unchanged to both grids. A mode
  passes if its growth rate changes by no more than the agreed tolerance and it stays at the
  pedestal on both grids.
- **When a mode stops.** A mode needs no further job once it has grown as far above its
  minimum as its fit window reached on the original grid.

## Memory and layout

The first job showed that one run on the doubled grid needs about 235 GB at its peak
([one linear run on the 160 × 256 grid peaks at 234–238 GB during its first step (270 GB with 4 processes × 32 threads), about four times the 80 × 128 run; two runs fit on one node]{.claim}[C-270](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-270){.cid .st-measured}), about four times the original grid's footprint. Only two runs fit on
one node. The job script therefore started the runs one at a time and held back the third,
as it was written to do. n = 20 now runs as a second chain on a node of its own.

The same jobs compared ways of splitting a run over 128 cores. Four processes with 32
threads each ran a step about twice as fast as two processes with 64 threads
([a linear step on the 160 × 256 grid takes 6.1 s with 4 processes × 32 threads, 11.2 s with 2 × 64 and 16 s with 2 × 32 (two runs per node); on 80 × 128 it takes 4.2 s with 2 × 16]{.claim}[C-271](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-271){.cid .st-measured}). Every later job uses four processes. About seven jobs in all are
expected, inside the number the owner approved.

## What is still open

The result. Until the chain ends, the case (b) growth rates are converged in time step
only.

Technical details → [JOREK](../technical/jorek.qmd#case-b-grid-check). Decision → [OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43).
